html:
The Karapana, who call themselves Muteamasa, are a small Tukanoan-speaking people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil, in the northwest Amazon. Like their neighbours the Tukano, Desano and Tariana, they live in riverside villages, once in great longhouses, and grow manioc and fish.

The Vaupés peoples follow a rule that a person must marry someone whose father's language is different from their own, so many people grow up speaking three or four languages. Missionaries and rubber collectors reached the region in the late 1800s and 1900s. See Colombia and manioc farmers.
